title: Surge absorbers and rollback heuristics: Incident triage and long-term actions for dedicated pool scaling regression
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a sustained traffic surge on 2025-03-04 we observed a progressive throughput shortfall in multiple Dedicated pools that impacted two enterprise customers. The immediate symptom was rising queue length and tail latency > SLA for 15-40 minutes despite autoscaler activity. This ticket captures the triage timeline, the working hypothesis for the regression, short-term mitigations applied, and the consolidated long-term action items to avoid recurrence. The incident surfaced interactions between a recent autoscaler debounce change, reduced configured headroom for certain reserved pools, and the new preemption policy introduced last quarter.

Observations: queue growth started at 08:42 UTC; autoscaler logs show scale decisions at 08:43 and 08:48 but pods/nodes came up late due to delayed preemption handshake with Dedicated controller. Headroom metrics dropped from target 22% to 6% after the change; KV-cache warmup time increased token latency for streaming requests, amplifying perceived load.

Working hypothesis: A combination of (1) debounce window extension in autoscaler PR#3458 that delayed reactive scale-ups under bursty signals; (2) an aggressive headroom override in customer templates that reduced the minimum reserved capacity, and (3) an interaction with the preemption negotiation that slowed pod readiness. Together these caused the autoscaler to react too late and with insufficient units, producing the shortfall.

Scope: Affects dedicated pools with reserved headroom overrides and autoscaler >= v2.4.1; not observed for fully-hosted ephemeral pools.
timeline: 2025-03-04 08:42 UTC: First alerts from synthetics and customer support about increased stream tail latency.
2025-03-04 08:44 UTC: On-call (SRE) paged; initial triage pinned to dedicated-pool churn and queue length metric.
2025-03-04 08:48 UTC: Autoscaler emitted scale-up events; nodes scheduled but readiness delayed by preemption handshake failures (kube events).
2025-03-04 09:10 UTC: Temporary action: increased reserved capacity for affected pools (+2 nodes) and disabled debounce override in autoscaler config; latency recovered within 7 minutes.
2025-03-04 11:00 UTC: Reverted autoscaler commit (PR#3458) in canary; added emergency circuit-breaker to bypass debounce for sustained queue signals.
2025-03-05 10:00 UTC: Post-incident working group: SRE, Runtime, Dedicated Product and Solutions Engs. Preliminary RCA drafted.
short_term_mitigations: Emergency capacity bump: manual +2 nodes in affected pools (applied at 08:52 UTC).
Rollback of autoscaler debounce extension (reverted PR#3458) in canary and then region-wide at 11:00 UTC.
Temporarily disable headroom override for 3 enterprise customers with custom templates; restored platform defaults.
Enabled circuit-breaker rule to force scale-up when queue depth > 3000 for >90s regardless of debounce.
Customer communications: support bulletin and dedicated post-incident email to impacted customers (sent 2025-03-04 12:05 UTC).
root_cause_analysis:
Primary root cause is the autoscaler debounce extension combined with lowered reserved headroom in a subset of dedicated pool templates. The debounce change (intended to reduce flapping) increased the minimum reaction time for scale-ups during bursty arrival patterns; coupled with reduced headroom the system lacked buffer capacity to absorb spikes. A secondary contributor was slower pod readiness caused by the preemption negotiation with the Dedicated controller (timeouts increased by 20s under load). No single-team change alone would have produced the full outage; the regression emerged from a cross-component interaction.

Evidence: autoscaler logs, kube events showing preemption delays, headroom_time_series (Grafana ID: dpool-headroom-2025-03-04), and customer traffic traces (S3 logs: s3://redwood-incident-archive/ENG-248314/).
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Rollback autoscaler debounce extension to restore reactive scale-up behavior. Tradeoff: increased risk of flapping in noisy microbursts; mitigated by adding a short-lived circuit-breaker and improved metric smoothing.
Decision: Reintroduce a conservative minimum headroom floor of 20% for reserved dedicated pools. Tradeoff: higher cost for reservation; rationale: SLA protection for enterprise customers.
Decision: Add readiness optimization work for preemption handshake rather than relaxing preemption safety. Tradeoff: engineering time and regression testing required before wide rollout.
action_items: ENG: Implement autoscaler deterministic fail-safe — bypass debounce when queue depth sustained > threshold (owner: Priya Mehta, estimate: 3, due: 2025-03-19).
SRE: Add runbook step to increase reserved headroom and how-to script for emergency capacity bump (owner: James O'Connor, estimate: 2, due: 2025-03-12).
Runtime: Improve preemption handshake path and reduce readiness timeout from 45s to 15s (owner: Linus Kramer, estimate: 8, due: 2025-04-02).
Product: Update Dedicated pool template defaults to enforce minimum headroom and document cost/benefit for customers (owner: Maria Gomez, estimate: 5, due: 2025-03-26).
QE: Create synthetic burst tests that cover 10-90th arrival percentile ramps and validate autoscaler behavior in canary (owner: Kunal Singh, estimate: 5, due: 2025-03-28).
Observability: Add a dedicated 'headroom alert' and enrich autoscaler metrics with correlation ids to traces (owner: SRE metrics team, estimate: 3, due: 2025-03-19).
Document: Post-incident report and runbook updates published to Confluence with clear rollback/playbook steps (owner: Aisha Patel, estimate: 2, due: 2025-03-14).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Autoscaler bypass rule merged and deployed to canary; verified with synthetic burst tests without violating flapping thresholds. 2) Minimum headroom policy enforced in new reserved templates. 3) Readiness timeout fix validated in staging with preemption feature flags. 4) Runbook and customer comms updated and approved by SRE and Product.
review_feedback: PM review (Maria Gomez): request clearer customer-facing cost impact estimates before enforcing headroom in templates — actioned by Product (linked doc).
SRE review (James O'Connor): suggested shorter rollback window during future canary tests; added to canary gating checklist.
Design review (API ergonomics): propose a controlled API for headroom overrides that surfaces warnings and requires approval for <20% values.
Security review: no secrets exposure; recommended minimal changes to KMS flows — no blockers.
notes: This incident highlights the risk of component-level optimizations (debounce) being safe in isolation but hazardous when combined with policy changes (headroom overrides). The long-term plan is to build tighter canary gates that run cross-team interaction tests (autoscaler + dedicated controller + template overrides) before merging autoscaler changes to main. Also prioritize better telemetry that correlates headroom, queue depth and readiness signals so SRE can triage faster.
synth_test_plan: QE will run a matrix of synthetic tests covering burst amplitude (x1.5, x3, x5), ramp duration (1s, 30s, 5m), and concurrent KV-cache cold starts. Results will be posted to the canary dashboard and compared against baseline (pre-PR3458) behaviour.
customer_communication: Initial notice and mitigation summary sent 2025-03-04 12:05 UTC; follow-up with RCA and action items planned for 2025-03-13. Support assigned point contacts for impacted customers until 2025-03-31.
provenance: Created from on-call logs, internal SRE notes, and cross-team RCA session March 5 2025. Drafted by Aisha Patel; technical validation by Linus Kramer and Priya Mehta.
